text: Foe is too quick, and you lose your chance to attack.
You trip over your own feet and lose the chance to attack.
Your mighty yell fails to impress your foes, but it leaves you a bit breathless. Take a -5 Fatigue penalty.
That move only works in a saga. Take 1d5 hits damage and suffer a -7 initiative penalty next round.
You lost your weapon! Wait, you weren't using one. Spend the next round Stunned.
Your move is acrobatic, but misjudged. You end up flat on your back and are Stunned for one round.
Execute the declared attack on the nearest ally, whoops! If no ally is in reach, an innocent bystander will do. Failing that, attack an imaginary friend.
You have trouble believing that your awesome kill move did not work at all. Spend two rounds Stunned by your failure.
The problem with using your body is a weapon is that sometime you hit something hard. You take 2d10 hits and are Stunned two rounds.
You execute a perfect blow, but your foe blocks it casually, perhaps accidentally; you are Stunned for two rounds by the shock of this.
Your foot slips out from under you as you begin your attack. You fall and Stun yourself for two rounds.
Your balance is a little off while requiring one foot to support your full weight. You suffer a -20 ankle sprain.
You miss and overextend, pulling something in your back. Pulled muscle is a -20 injury. Take 2d10 hits and a round of Stun from the pain.
You execute a textbook headbutt... to the ground. You are prone, Stunned for three rounds, and bleeding 1/rnd.
